tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, ensure the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg and that the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever constructing a move, check that the source peg has the disk on top and that the move does not place a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 from a peg where disk 2 is on top, or moving disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Leverage the smallest disk (disk 1) as a temporary holder because it can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is blocked by a smaller one, move the smallest disk to a free peg to free the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 2 onto a peg that has disk 1 on top, causing a size violation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, leave them untouched and build the remaining tower on top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target peg already has correctly placed larger disks, avoid moving them and only add smaller disks above.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 off the goal peg when it is already at the bottom of the final tower.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Place disks onto the goal peg one by one in descending size order (largest remaining to smallest), ensuring each larger disk is placed before any smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final tower, move the next largest disk onto the goal peg after clearing its path.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 2 onto the goal peg before moving disk 4, which would block the larger disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the last syntactically correct list of moves in the response is the complete move sequence; no other list should appear after it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the answer, place the move list at the very end of the response and avoid any additional brackets or lists afterward.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending an empty list [] after the move list, causing the parser to read the empty list as the answer.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration matches goal before outputting
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Mentally simulate each move from the initial configuration and confirm that the final state exactly matches the goal before publishing the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After constructing the move sequence, replay the moves mentally (or on paper) to ensure the goal is reached.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on a non‑goal peg because the final configuration was not checked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive sub‑tower transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a destination peg using the third peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the k‑1 disks onto the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When needing to relocate an entire sub‑tower of consecutive disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move a stack of three disks directly without first moving the top two to the auxiliary peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid blocking future moves with temporary placements
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When using a disk as a temporary buffer, place it on a peg that will not need to be cleared for later moves, preventing unnecessary extra moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When selecting a temporary peg for a small disk, choose one that won't be required as a source or destination for larger disks later.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 1 on the goal peg early, which then blocks moving larger disks onto that peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk onto it
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg, ensure the peg is empty or its current top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk needs to be placed onto a peg that currently holds smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure final move list is the last list in the response
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Place the move list as the very last list in the output; do not include any additional list (even an empty one) after it, because the verifier parses the last list as the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When finalizing the answer, output the move list and then stop; avoid any trailing brackets, empty lists, or other list literals.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending [] after the move list, causing the parser to read [] as the answer and reject the solution.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation before emitting the required list, often because it assumes the answer is implicit or due to premature termination.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a non‑empty list of moves as the final output, even if the solution is trivial.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on moving the correct disk but forgets to check the destination peg's top disk size.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on its target location without confirming it is the topmost disk on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the top element of its source peg before adding the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Generation may be cut off by token limits or by an early stop token, leaving the move list unfinished.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Count moves mentally or on paper and ensure the list ends with a closing bracket; if needed, shorten the solution but keep it complete.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of disk locations during multi‑step reasoning and references an incorrect source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit mental (or written) representation of each peg's contents after every move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Including extra list after the final move list, causing the parser to select the wrong list
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model often adds a trailing empty list or another list for formatting, not realizing the verifier extracts the last list as the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After writing the move list, stop outputting any further list literals; ensure the move list is the final syntactic list in the response.
